geology: Lithium-cesium-tantalum (LCT) granitic pegmatites; primary hard-rock Li source (Greenbushes, Pilbara).
extraction: Decrepitation (alpha->beta conversion ~1050 C) then acid roast with concentrated H2SO4 ~250 C to form water-soluble Li2SO4, water leach, remove Mg/Ca/Fe, precipitate Li2CO3 with Na2CO3 (or convert to LiOH).
notes: Formula equivalently LiAlSi2O6. Dominant hard-rock route; beta phase expands ~30% making ore acid-reactive.

geology: Granitic pegmatites; lower Li grade than spodumene, prized for low-iron glass/ceramics.
extraction: Decrepitation then sulfuric acid roast, water leach and precipitation similar to spodumene.

geology: Li-mica in evolved pegmatites; carries rubidium and cesium credits.
extraction: Sulfate or chloride roast, leach, solvent extraction / ion exchange for Rb/Cs separation, precipitate Li2CO3.
notes: Fluorine content complicates processing; Rb/Cs recovered as byproducts.

geology: Closed-basin salars (Atacama, Hombre Muerto, Uyuni); most abundant Li resource.
extraction: Solar evaporation ponds concentrate brine (>90% water lost), remove Mg/Ca by precipitation, then precipitate battery-grade Li2CO3 with Na2CO3. DLE/ion-exchange sorption is an emerging alternative.
notes: Salar de Atacama supplies >40% of global lithium.

geology: Granitic pegmatites and some metamorphic rocks; ~4-5% Be in industrial beryl.
extraction: Melt and quench (frit) to make ore acid-reactive, grind, react with H2SO4, leach, solvent extraction, precipitate Be(OH)2.
final_product: Be(OH)2 -> Be metal / BeO / Cu-Be alloy
notes: Beryl must be fritted/quenched before acid attack; inert otherwise.

geology: Volcanic tuff deposits (Spor Mountain, Utah); dominant mined Be source despite low grade (<0.5% Be).
extraction: Sulfuric acid leach near boiling, solvent extraction (D2EHPA in kerosene), ammonium carbonate complexation, precipitate Be(OH)2 (SX-carbonate process).
notes: Leached directly without fritting, unlike beryl.

geology: LCT pegmatites and alluvial placers; also recovered from tin slags.
extraction: Digest concentrate in hydrofluoric acid to form soluble heptafluoride complexes, solvent extraction with MIBK separates Ta from Nb, precipitate K2TaF7 / Ta2O5 and Nb2O5, refine to metal.
notes: Columbite is Nb-rich, tantalite Ta-rich; HF + MIBK SX is the standard industrial separation.

geology: Carbonatite complexes (Araxa Brazil, Niobec Canada); dominant Nb source.
extraction: Concentrate reduced aluminothermically or silicothermically with Fe2O3 to ferroniobium for steel; HF route gives purified Nb2O5/Nb metal.
notes: Bulk of world Nb is sold as FeNb for HSLA steel; formula approx (Na,Ca)2Nb2O6(OH,F).

geology: Sedimentary/hydrothermal carbonate deposits; also refractory MgO source.
extraction: Calcine to MgO then silicothermic (Pidgeon) reduction with ferrosilicon under vacuum ~1200 C; Mg vapor condenses as crown metal.
notes: Alternative raw material to dolomite in the Pidgeon process.

geology: Abundant sedimentary carbonate; main Pidgeon-process feedstock.
extraction: Calcine to dolime then silicothermic reduction with ferrosilicon under vacuum (Pidgeon); CaO scavenges silica. Alternatively convert to MgCl2 and electrolyze.
notes: >80% of global primary Mg is Pidgeon silicothermic from dolomite.

geology: Seawater, salt-lake and well brines; effectively inexhaustible Mg source.
extraction: Precipitate Mg(OH)2 with lime/dolime, convert to MgCl2 with HCl, dehydrate, electrolyze molten MgCl2 to Mg metal + Cl2.
notes: Classic electrolytic route (Dow); power-intensive, used where cheap electricity/brine exist.

geology: Rare mineral in zoned LCT pegmatites (Tanco, Manitoba; Bikita, Zimbabwe); primary Cs source.
extraction: Acid digestion (HCl or H2SO4) and leach, remove silica, precipitate/ion-exchange to CsCl or Cs alum; Rb separated by fractional crystallisation or SX.
notes: Hydrated form (Cs,Na)AlSi2O6.H2O; cesium formate drilling fluid is a key product. Rb has no economic primary ore and is recovered here and from lepidolite.

geology: Heavy-mineral-sand placers alongside ilmenite/rutile; the primary Zr source.
extraction: Carbothermic reduction to ZrC/ZrN then chlorination to ZrCl4 (with ~2% HfCl4); solvent extraction (MIBK-thiocyanate or TBP) separates Hf for nuclear-grade Zr; Kroll (Mg) reduction of tetrachloride to sponge, then refine.
final_product: Zr sponge metal; Hf metal; ZrO2
notes: Hf (~2% of Zr) must be removed for reactor-grade Zr due to high neutron cross-section; most zircon used as sand/opacifier/ZrO2 rather than reduced.

geology: No primary ore; recovered from Bayer alumina liquor and zinc processing.
extraction: Recovered by solvent extraction / ion exchange / electrolysis from Bayer liquor or zinc residues.
notes: Cross-link only: model as byproduct of aluminium (bauxite) and zinc chains, not an independent ore.

geology: No primary ore; recovered from sphalerite (ZnS) refining residues and flue dusts (Ge also from coal fly ash).
extraction: Recovered from zinc refining residues by leaching, solvent extraction and precipitation.
notes: Cross-link only: byproduct of the zinc chain.

geology: No primary ore; recovered from copper electrorefining anode slimes.
extraction: Roast/leach copper anode slimes, precipitate and refine Se and Te.
notes: Cross-link only: byproduct of the copper chain.

geology: No primary ore; recovered from MoS2 roaster flue dust, itself a Cu-porphyry byproduct.
extraction: Scrub roaster flue gas, recover perrhenate by ion exchange/solvent extraction, reduce to Re metal.
notes: Cross-link only: byproduct of the molybdenum/copper chain.
